name: Papasena

earlier_scan.note: Only wordlists (Voorhoeve 1975, Briley 1978, McAllister 1986, Menanti & Rumaropen 2022); no phonology/grammar

readall_conflicts: No disagreement between sources about a stated rule, because no source states one. The only prosodic evidence for Papasena is McAllister's 1986 survey sheet, which marks a prominence tick in varying positions (initial in some words, second syllable in others, two ticks in some) and annotates one monosyllabic minimal pair for low vs high tone. Whether the tick records stress or pitch is not said. Clouse 1997 (already logged in by the earlier reading, not in this work list) speaks only at family level, explicitly excluding Papasena for lack of data: 'Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages' (p.152) and stress 'has not been found to be contrastive in any of the Lakes Plain languages to date' (p.160). The tone annotation on the wordlist is consistent with that family-level picture; the variable ticks neither confirm nor refute it.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane A. 1997. Towards a reconstruction and reclassification of the Lakes Plain languages of Irian Jaya. In Karl Franklin (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 2 (Pacific Linguistics A-85), 133-236. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A85.133; hdl:1885/253630.
sources.note: Papasena explicitly excluded from the study for lack of data (p.134); family-level only: p.152 'Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages.. All the modern languages have at least high and low tone'; p.160 (Appendix 3 note) 'stress is not marked because only a few original word lists marked it and it has not been found to be contrastive in any of the Lakes Plain languages to date'. No Papasena wordlist in the appendix; Papasena appears only in the East Tariku tree (p.155).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-B31; hdl:1885/146481.
sources.note: Checklist entry '84. PAPASENA, IXa, Village: Papasena, Source: U13' (U13 = missionary survey wordlists) and a 40-item comparative list '84. PAPASENA (Br)' in the appendix; no phonological notes, no stress or tone marks anywhere (the string 'stress' occurs nowhere in the volume).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid papa1269 and reference record 665313 (Hammarström et al.).
sources.note: Nine references, all overview or wordlist type (Voorhoeve 1975 x2, Sugono 2008, Menanti & Rumaropen 2022, McAllister 1986, Briley 1978, Manning 1978, Cooper 1978); zero descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references.

sources.citation: Menanti, Jacqualine & Ben Rumaropen. 2022. Survey Report on the Kapauri Language of Papua, Indonesia. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-026. SIL International. 69 pp. Appendix B.4 (pp.41-48) = scanned handwritten 'Ari' (Papasena) wordlist, L. McAllister, Papasena village, 18 April 1986 (= McAllister 1986b, SIL archive 69145).
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; the words stress/tone/accent/pitch never occur; p.23 says all appendix data are unanalysed field transcriptions. The scanned McAllister wordlist (viewed pp.41-42) carries a hand-written stress tick on most Papasena items, in varying positions (ˈtaɽu 'boil', aˈpu 'buttocks', akuˈta 'chest', ˈaikipu 'elbow', ˈawa 'eye', ˈkitawig 'ant', kwaˈaɽu 'fly', ˈkug 'tree'); no rule stated.

sources.citation: Yoder, Brendon. 2020. A grammar of Abawiri, a Lakes Plain language of Papua, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, UC Santa Barbara. Sections 1.3-1.4 (pp.9-12).
sources.note: About Papasena only that it is 'not mentioned in all Clouse's work' but always placed in East Tariku; the inventory of existing Lakes Plain descriptions (Iau, Doutai, Edopi, Obokuitai, Sikaritai, Kirikiri, Fayu, Abawiri) contains nothing on Papasena. Family remark: 'All of these languages are tonal'. Nothing on Papasena stress.

sources.citation: McAllister, Lawrence. 1986b. Papasena wordlist from Papasena village ('Ari'). Abepura: SIL. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 69145 (scan reproduced as Appendix B.4 of Menanti & Rumaropen 2022, pp.41-48).
sources.note: The only Papasena primary record with any prosodic marking: hand-written stress ticks on ~250 items. A careful read of all 8 scanned pages (only pp.41-42 inspected here) could give a distributional statement of the tick position, though the transcriber gave no rule and the marks may be pitch rather than stress in a tonal family.

sources.citation: Briley, David. 1978. 'Ari' survey wordlist, Daude village (Papasena I, pop. 275), Kec. Tor Atas, informant Anton (29), 14 April 1978. 5 pp. (65 entries; p.5 handwritten field notes). SIL Language & Culture Archives item 69264.
sources.note: No phonology content. Stress ticks on most forms (agaˈudalu? 'shoulder', aˈta 'finger', aˈtita 'head', ˈtaui 'child', taˈga 'dog', ˈpai 'crocodile', ˈderi 'fish', ˈpi 'louse', tɛˈgɔ 'boy', tuˈgɔ 'girl'), position varying; p.5 notes are sociolinguistic only ('There's a small village next door called Bari / Isn't same as Tareve / Can hear not speak Iri, Sikari / Papasena only'). Marks only, no statement.

sources.citation: Cooper, Dianne. 1978. Papasena 1 ('Taeri') survey wordlist, Papasena Satu village, Kec. Tor Atas, informant Towas, 14 April 1978. 4 pp. (173-item Irian Jaya survey form, 92 entries filled). SIL Language & Culture Archives item 69143.
sources.note: No phonology content (handwritten survey wordlist). Prosodic MARKS only: a raised stress tick before a syllable on most items, mostly word-initial (ˈakaųta 'shoulder', ˈawari 'meat', ˈaru 'tail', ˈari 'tooth', ˈapɔluta 'nose', ˈawa 'eye', ˈtaka 'termite', ˈkwari 'worm', ˈderi 'fish', ˈkwaru 'fly', ˈwaru 'rain', ˈatuŋ 'knee', ˈawe 'mouth', ˈaki 'stomach') but also non-initial (aˈtita 'head', aˈbaritu 'skin', aˈtɔru 'wing', aiˈwitɔ 'ear', tɛˈhɔ 'boy', taˈwi 'child'); the transcriber wrote the word 'tone' beside segmentally identical items -- 6 gigi/tooth 'ari tone', 10 kaki/foot 'arɔ Tone', 14…

sources.citation: Cooper, Dianne. 1978. Papasena 2 survey wordlist (list A), Papasena 2 village (18 houses), Kec. Tor Atas, informant Bernard (40), 17 April 1978. 4 pp., 49 entries. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 69144.
sources.note: No phonology content. Stress ticks, again mostly initial (ˈtai 'blood', ˈari 'tooth', aˈlali 'meat', aˈtida 'head', ˈawa 'eye', ˈtaka 'dog', ˈpi 'louse', aiˈyɛta 'hand') with some non-initial; no key, no statement.

sources.citation: Manning, Margaret. 1978. Papasena II survey wordlist (list B), Papasena II village (100+ people, 18 houses), Kec. Tor Atas, informant Bernard, 17 April 1978. 4 pp., 48 entries. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 69142.
sources.note: No phonology content. Stress ticks on most items in varying positions (ˈawa 'eye', ˈawararu 'face', ˈatɔru 'wing', ˈawitɔ 'ear', ˈdɛri 'fish' vs aˈri 'tooth', a'ri 'neck', aˈrɛrɛ 'tongue', ayapɔˈru 'finger'); háček-like marks over some vowels; pp.2-4 largely blank; 'Explanation of Symbols' empty. Marks only, no statement.
